name: plan-phases-project-scoping
body:
`apg_plan_phases` (the suite tool `opencode-suite/tools/apg_plan_phases.ts`) must report only the requirements the CURRENT project / branch is responsible for, not every requirement in the layers store. Today it loads all `Requirement` nodes (line 41: `MATCH (r:Requirement) RETURN r.fqn`) and flags any without a `Satisfies` edge as unsatisfied (line 82). A project's plan is transient and dies with its branch, so requirements delivered by earlier projects keep no surviving `Satisfies` edge and read unsatisfied forever (observed in apg-cleanup: 24-25 previously-delivered requirements). The tool must scope the requirement set to the project.

IN SCOPE (decided): a requirement is in scope for the current project/branch when it is BRANCH-ADDED or is SATISFIED by one of this project's phases — in-scope = branch-added requirements ∪ requirements this project's phases Satisfy. Branch-added mirrors the binary's `solution_nodes_added_on_branch` (`rust.apg.plan_cmd.verify.solution_nodes_added_on_branch`, `src/plan_cmd/verify.rs` lines 240-287): a `apg/layers/requirements/requirement/<name>.json` node file present on this branch but absent from the repo's default branch. The suite tool may shell out to git to compute this (the shared lib already runs subprocesses via `Bun.$` for `apg query`). The design splits cleanly across the test tiers: the scoping DECISION is a PURE function in the shared `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` — given the full requirement FQN set, the branch-added set, and this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs, it returns the in-scope set and the findings — and is covered by the bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out is a thin subprocess WRAPPER around that pure core (a subprocess is real I/O, hence e2e, not unit) and is covered by the opt-in suite e2e. The tool's top-level logic is a default-exported `tool({...})` and cannot be unit-tested directly, which is why the pure core lives in the shared lib.

FINDINGS after the change:
- Preserved unchanged: `!! no tasks`; `!! done but under review`; `!! Gates cycle detected`.
- `!! unsatisfied requirements` = in-scope requirements with no `Satisfies` from a phase of THIS project (equivalently, branch-added requirements the project's plan does not satisfy).
- `!! <req> Satisfied by more than one phase` = requirements Satisfied by more than one phase OF THIS PROJECT (the `Satisfies` lookup is filtered to this project's phases).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Running `apg_plan_phases` in a project whose branch adds no requirement and whose plan satisfies its own requirements reports NO unsatisfied finding for requirements delivered by other projects; the in-scope set is exactly {requirements added on this branch} ∪ {requirements this project's phases Satisfy}.
- A branch-added requirement with no satisfying phase is still reported unsatisfied; a requirement satisfied by two phases of the project is still reported over-satisfied.
- The no-tasks, done-but-under-review and Gates-cycle findings are unchanged.
- Test tiers, split exactly: the PURE scoping core in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` (requirement FQNs + branch-added set + this project's `Satisfies` phase FQNs -> in-scope set and findings) is covered by the side-effect-free bun unit tier in `opencode-suite/lib/apg.test.ts`; the git branch-delta shell-out wrapper is covered by the opt-in suite e2e (`opencode-suite/tests/boundary.e2e.test.ts`) against a scratch `/tmp` repo per `global.constraint.no-real-project-test`. No subprocess-dependent path is claimed at the unit tier.
- The two existing Rust e2e regressions stay green: `full_dogfood_round_trip_suite_tool_ops_inside_the_worktree` (`tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`) and `suite_tools_query_error_guard_is_structural` (`tests/main_e2e.rs`, which structurally pins `apg_plan_phases.ts`'s try/catch/`csvToRows`/return shape); the scoping change must not regress either.
- Non-goal: no change to the `apg` binary and no change to suite tools other than `apg_plan_phases` and the shared-lib helper it uses (see `requirements.constraint.plan-tooling-change-boundary`).

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE: `opencode-suite/agents/plan-writer.md` (line 213) relies on `apg_plan_phases` reporting unsatisfied requirements for its self-review; with this scoping that check becomes project-local, which is the point. No agent-guidance change is required by this change-set.
